**The first stable release since 1.1.0.** Everything between them shipped as prereleases while the murder engine was being built and tested at the table, which is why `releases/latest` kept pointing at 1.1.0. This one is the real thing: install from the manifest and you get this.

115 commits since 1.1.0. The short version of what changed.

## Murders that finish properly

The incident engine grew up. An accomplice who walks in can now turn on the killer, and that betrayal opens as its own incident with its own opening roll, so one night can leave two bodies and the trial has two killings to untangle. Nobody walks out of an incident they are standing in except through a crisis action. Stage 6 became worth attempting: covering your tracks, reshaping a trace into something innocent, moving the body, and a Tamper Remnant that admits somebody handled it and lies about everything else. Deaths by one's own hand skip the confrontation and go straight to the arrangements.

## Despair Overflow

Despair that will not fit in a full pool used to evaporate. A season run measured two thirds of the income dying that way. It now collects in a counter shared by every Monokuma, and when it reaches its threshold one thing is drawn at random from eight: darker Eclipses, fewer search tokens, fewer actions, no Hope, no Hope Calls, no free Move, worn equipment, or projects set back. It lasts one time of day. A Monokuma can also pour Despair in on purpose.

## The day

Action budgets come back when the Eclipse opens rather than when it ends, so a murder declared in the dark is paid for out of the day it belongs to. Items have durability, and Despair on a roll wears down the tool that was used. Nothing is deleted because a chapter ended: clearing Faint Remnants and sweeping Truth Bullets are the GM's own tools now.

## The case

The investigation dashboard reads traces three ways and keeps the reading. A trace and the Truth Bullets taken from it are one record, editable from either end. Traces are tied to the murder by what happened rather than by what they are. Every objection in a trial takes a different track from the objection playlist.

## The school

Doorway glow never runs wider than the doorway. Diagonal walls close the staircases drawn along them. Room outlines stop drawing blobs where a wall was too short to draw as a line. `diagnoseFog`, `whatIsHere` and `doorwayReport` say what the map is actually doing.

## Fixed in 1.2.0 itself

A critical was paying three Hope for a guide that says two. Two mechanisms were implementing the same rule at once: the older one topped up the system's single point from the chat hook, the newer one made the duality funnel pay the full amount. Both were live. Measured end to end, a critical action took Hope from 0 to 3; it takes it to 2 now, and an ordinary Hope roll still pays 1. The reroll path still tops up by hand, because a reroll settles its resources somewhere this module does not wrap.

One editorial pass over every string the game shows. The things that were actually wrong: the Gear group was labelled "Tools", which is also one of the three categories inside it; its tooltip promised three shared slots when the rule has been two for a while, and it reads the real limit now; Clean-up told you that you had two actions when Wounded leaves you one; "18+" on the Misleading trail read as an age rating rather than a threshold; Season setup called Breakdown "Broken Down"; two singular forms were copies of their plural, so you could be told about "one of your 1 Truth Bullets"; four failures told a player to look in the browser console, which is not something a player can act on.

## Under the hood

The regression suite is 111 checks across three tiers, including a tier that reads the module's own source for code that says one thing and does another. Run it with `game.drpg.runTests()`.

This release was reviewed by running the module headlessly on three simultaneous clients, one GM and two players, against a mock of Foundry that keeps the real permission rules and refuses writes a real server would refuse. The full report is in `audit/` in the repository, including one finding left open on purpose: the incident's killer id lives in a world setting, so a player who opens the console during a class trial can read it. Nothing in the interface shows it, and fixing it properly means moving the identity onto the channel that already carries the module's other secrets. That is a change for its own release, not a footnote in this one.

## Installing

```
https://github.com/Akrobacjum/Danganronpa-RPG/releases/latest/download/module.json
```

Needs Foundry v14 (14.364+), the Daggerheart system 2.6.0+, and Dice So Nice, Isometric Perspective and LiveKit AVClient. The module refuses to start without them and says which one is missing.
